facts.statement: The genus Prenoceratops was named by Chinnery in 2004.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Chinnery, 2004

facts.statement: Prenoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The name Prenoceratops means 'bent or prone-horned face' and comes from Greek words for bent, horn, and face.
facts.quote: Prenoceratops, (meaning 'bent or prone-horned face' and derived from Greek prene-/πρηνη- meaning 'bent forwards' or 'prone', cerat-/κερατ- meaning 'horn' and -ops/ωψ meaning 'face')

facts.statement: Prenoceratops was a small dinosaur that grew to about 1.3 meters long and weighed 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small dinosaur, reaching 1.3 m in length and 20 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Fossils of Prenoceratops were found in the Campanian-age Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dating to 74.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the upper Two Medicine Formation in the present-day U.S. state of Montana, in Campanian age rock layers that have been dated to 74.3 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Prenoceratops were also found in the Oldman Formation in Alberta, Canada, dating to around 77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils were also found in the Oldman Formation in the modern day Canadian province of Alberta, dating to around 77 million years ago.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops was first discovered on a Blackfeet reservation in Pondera County, Montana.
facts.quote: Prenoceratops was first discovered on a Blackfeet reservation in Pondera County, Montana in layers coming from the Campanian Two Medicine Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, designated TCM 2003.1.1, includes a surangular fused with an articular.
facts.quote: The holotype was one of the few associated specimens, including a surrangular fused with an articular, the specimen is designated as TCM 2003.1.1.

facts.statement: Brenda J. Chinnery described Prenoceratops in 2004.
facts.quote: Prenoceratops was later described by Brenda J. Chinnery in 2004, though the taxon has been little noticed since.

facts.statement: An isolated right frontal bone from the Oldman Formation in Alberta was described in 2010 and assigned to Prenoceratops.
facts.quote: An isolated right frontal from the Oldman Formation of southern Alberta, Canada was described in 2010 and ascribed to Prenoceratops as P. sp.

facts.statement: The only known species of Prenoceratops is P. pieganensis.
facts.quote: Named Prenoceratops species include only P. pieganensis (type).

facts.statement: Prenoceratops is closely related to Leptoceratops and lived several million years before it.
facts.quote: It is closely related to Leptoceratops, which it antedates by several million years.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Prenoceratops, like all ceratopsians, was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Because flowering plants were geographically limited during the Cretaceous, Prenoceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: During the Cretaceous, flowering plants were "geographically limited on the landscape", and so it is likely that this dinosaur fed on the predominant plants of the era: ferns, cycads and conifers.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops used its sharp beak to bite off leaves or needles.
facts.quote: It would have used its sharp ceratopsian beak to bite off the leaves or needles.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops pieganensis lived during the Upper Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Prenoceratops pieganensis belongs to the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Prenoceratops pieganensis lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 74 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 74 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops measured approximately 1.50 meters in length and 70 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: Prenoceratops medía aproximadamente 1,50 metro de largo y 70 centímetros de alto.

facts.statement: Prenoceratops had a wide, thick skull with a parrot-like beak used to cut ferns, cycads, and conifers, which it then chewed with its back teeth.
facts.quote: Su cráneo, ancho y grueso, presentaba en un pico similar al de los loros, con el cual cortaba los helechos, cicadeas y coníferas de la que se alimentaba, estando las plantas con flores limitadas geográficamente, para luego masticarlos con los dientes posteriores.

facts.statement: The time range for Prenoceratops is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Prenoceratops is unusual because it is the only basal neoceratopsian known from a bonebed containing a large number of fossil elements.
rejected.quote: It is unusual in that it is the only basal neoceratopsian known from a bonebed and the sheer number of elements.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'it is the only basal neoceratopsian known from'

rejected.statement: Prenoceratops belonged to the Ceratopsia, a group of herbivorous dinosaurs with parrot-like beaks that lived in North America and Asia during the Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Prenoceratops belonged to the Ceratopsia (which name is derived from Ancient Greek, meaning 'horned face'), a group of herbivorous dinosaurs with parrot-like beaks, which thrived in North America and Asia during the Cretaceous Period.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a group of herbivorous dinosaurs with parrot-like beaks'

rejected.statement: Prenoceratops is characterized by a lower, more sloping head compared to Leptoceratops.
rejected.quote: It is characterized by a lower, more sloping head than that of Leptoceratops.
